interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: the phantom log claim left by an accepted InstallSnapshot changes how a server decides votes, and the same starvation blocks configuration changes whose new quorum would include such a server, wedging further configuration changes behind the blocked one. Vote half, decided by a retained receipt with all four comparisons complete and holding (execution ca11633cbde949dba0da0b9950651148; setup index 0, probe index 1): the shared prefix ends at 42, the deposed leader and one follower hold an uncommitted suffix to 82 in term 2, the majority leader's snapshot sits at 63 in term 3, so both minority members cache a claim (82, term 2) above an installed snapshot (63, term 3) while a majority voter keeps a consistent claim (63, term 3). One RequestVote with term 4 and the candidate's real claim, carrying the leadership-transfer flag, was granted by the phantom (response term 4) and rejected by the consistent voter (response term 4, granted false), and the granted authority rested on entries the voter's snapshot had superseded. Config-change half, retained raw witnesses (execution 3c77f645320547ba8beb93c42ef5d9be; phantom case setup index 0 and probe index 1, consistent case setup index 2 and probe index 3): with identical phantom premises, removing a phantom voter committed in 0 ms and reduced the configuration from 5 to 4 voters, while removing a consistent follower did not commit within 5001 ms; the comparison-level association for these two predicates is unknown only because the probe event lacked an identity field present in its admission event, which the requested successor corrects. Source basis: a newly appended configuration is committed under the new configuration's quorum, because appendConfigurationEntry installs it into the commitment before the entry commits (src_append_config, raft.go 1204-1243), and a phantom holder cannot acknowledge any AppendEntries because its cached claim fails every prev-log check (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606, with the claim supplied by src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174, and left stale by installSnapshot, src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977). Wedge: after the blocked change the leader's latest configuration never committed, so the gate that admits further configuration requests stays closed; local construction runs of the new follow-up probe show the operator's next attempt (removing the phantom, the escape that would restore a consistent quorum) refused with a 1000 ms enqueue timeout and never committed within the following 2 s. That protective side also bounds the safety reading: the steps that would shrink the voter set down to the phantom group cannot commit, so the phantom grant cannot be converted into authority over committed entries through configuration changes in the measured history. Limits: the wedge and the corrected config-change comparisons await their receipt (currently construction feedback and raw retained values respectively); configuration changes attempted before the phantom state arises, repeated phantom generations, other cluster sizes and production-style monotonic stores are unmeasured; the leader's reported configuration size after a blocked change reflects the locally adopted latest configuration, not the committed one.
counterevidence: The parent question's repair probe shows the phantom claim is transient within a term: once a snapshot above the claim is published the follower is consistent again, so both the vote effect and the config-change effect end at that boundary.

The blocked configuration change is also protective: the steps that would shrink the voter set down to the phantom group cannot commit, so the phantom grant cannot become authority over committed entries through a configuration change in the measured history.

The blocked removal's failure is not leader saturation: the phantom removal committed in 0 ms under the same scenario, snapshot index, timing and load, so the difference tracks the composition of the new configuration's quorum rather than leader health.
The vote candidate is a real node with a real log claim (both minority members hold the same suffix); the only supplied element is the leadership-transfer flag on its request.
limitations: The corrected config-change comparisons and the follow-up wedge are requested with this update; only raw event values and local construction feedback support them so far.
A blocked removal leaves the leader with a locally adopted latest configuration that never committed, and the wedge it causes is measured only for the immediate follow-up request.
Configuration changes attempted before the phantom state arises, repeated phantom generations, other cluster sizes and production-style monotonic stores are unmeasured.

scope.description: The same two-case configuration-change probe on the validated five-voter phantom history, with the probe events now carrying the phantom identity and, when a removal is blocked, a follow-up removal attempt. Case one removes a phantom voter; case two removes a consistent follower; in case two a further RemoveServer for the phantom holder is then attempted with a one-second enqueue timeout and awaited for two seconds.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; induced events are one partition of two voters from three, retention of the minority suffix, one explicit snapshot, and the RemoveServer attempts.

Both cases keep history, snapshot index, timing and leader load identical so the removed voter's role is the only difference; the follow-up attempt uses the ordinary public API with the documented enqueue timeout.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting stays disabled so the published snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

experiment.prefix: Each case repeats the phantom setup (elect, commit forty entries, partition the leader with one follower, drive forty uncommitted applies on the deposed leader, wait for the pair to stop leading, wait for a majority leader, commit twenty entries and force Snapshot(), heal, wait for both minority members to install the snapshot), records the premise, then issues RemoveServer for the phantom holder or for a consistent follower and waits up to five seconds. When the first removal does not commit, a second RemoveServer for the phantom holder is issued with a one-second enqueue timeout and awaited for two seconds, and both outcomes are emitted.
semantic_changes: ca_config_probe now emits phantom_id and second_phantom_id so the admission event and the result event share an identity.
A blocked configuration change is followed by a second RemoveServer for the phantom holder, emitted as ca_config_probe2 with the enqueue outcome and a two-second commit window.
experiment.requirement: A configuration change must either commit or fail observably within a bounded time rather than block indefinitely because a voter whose cached log claim was superseded by its own snapshot can no longer accept log entries, and a blocked change must not prevent the operator from issuing further configuration changes.

comparisons.description: Removing a phantom voter commits promptly: the remaining configuration still contains three voters that accept entries.
Removing a consistent voter does not commit within the window: the new configuration's quorum includes a phantom holder, so the entry cannot gather its acknowledgements.
After the blocked change the operator's follow-up removal of the phantom holder is refused at enqueue time, so the wedge is not limited to the blocked entry itself.
The follow-up change also does not commit within its window, matching the closed configuration-change gate.

experiment.revision_reason: Both config-change comparisons resolved unknown because the probe event carried no identity field present in its admission event, so the alias could not be associated; the probe now emits phantom_id and second_phantom_id, and both comparisons use phantom_id. The blocked case also gained a follow-up RemoveServer for the phantom holder with the ordinary enqueue timeout, giving the wedge its own comparison subjects. Scenario, timing, anchors and the phantom premise are unchanged, and the earlier cases stay in the file.
